title: Browser administrator project-settings entry omits the initiating actor at Runtime startup
originalResult: Real Gateway browser authentication against an isolated current PostgreSQL schema; commit administrator demotion after authentication and before InstanceManager admission. The settings request returns302, omits the initiating administrator and physically allocates a new live LocalLauncher process for another administrator project. A separate earlier warm-reuse observation is not counted as a physical allocation.
correction: The settings entry forwards passive intent and the server-authenticated administrator id to the existing InstanceManager authorization and allocation path. Omitted actors remain reserved for trusted internal lifecycle work. The existing explicit-start requirement after a manual stop is retained.

actualGateway.result: Current and restored administrators start actual signed-readiness local processes. Role, disabled/deleted account, disabled/missing membership and disabled organization after authentication return403 without process allocation or selection-cookie writes. Warm reuse succeeds for current authority; manual-stop navigation returns409 without waking the Runtime.

normalNodeArtifacts.productionModules: Unchanged ordinary full Gateway tsc output; three checked test support files are emitted separately as ESM.

coverageQualification.changedCall: Real route-to-allocation execution covers current cold start, warm reuse, six queued authority refusals, restored eligibility and manual-stop policy. The relay JSON publication path and malformed JSON refusal are exercised.
coverageQualification.testLaneRegistration: Added only to the existing PostgreSQL lane and excluded from the keyless no-database lane.

intermediateCorrections: The first cold-start setup used idle stop, which correctly retained the Runtime without an idle-resource decision; the physical counterproof instead uses confirmed failed-stop cleanup.
The public fixture was aligned with the existing structured INSTANCE_STOPPED error rather than changing the response.
Checked test support requires an explicit ESM compiler mode when emitted without a package-aware project; the failed external artifact attempt is retained.
An initial fixture parse failure and optional native-handle type errors are retained and corrected without production compiler changes.
limits: Native acceptance is macOS with an owned PostgreSQL18.4 x86_64-apple-darwin binary; Linux account provisioning and native Windows supervision remain separate acceptance.

The assembled fixture owns real browser authentication, PostgreSQL, signed readiness and local process lifetime. It does not call a model provider or prove containment of arbitrary escaped descendants.
Global documentation quick-pass debt remains recorded from the earlier repository run; only the affected pairs and links are accepted here.
All12 audit domains remain in progress; paid real Responses validation stays deferred by explicit user instruction.
